title: Cap. II Arg. 2: praescientia loci (Rom. 8:29–30 / 11:2 / 1 Pet. 1:2)
pass_a_gloss: Secondly, those places are urged in which election or predestination unto glory is joined in express words with foreknowledge. As Rom. viii. 29, 30. Whom he foreknew, them he also predestinated to be conformed to the image of his Son, &c. And Rom. xi. 2. God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew. And 1 Pet. i. 2. To the elect strangers according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, unto sanctification of the Spirit, &c. From these and the like places the adversaries infer that God elected unto glory those whom he foreknew would be conformed to the image of his Son, that is, holy and good; so that this foreknowledge of future goodness or holiness was the cause of election unto glory.
pass_b_english: Second: they press the places where election or predestination to glory is joined in so many words with foreknowledge — Rom. 8:29–30 ("Whom he foreknew, he also predestined to be conformed to his Son's image…"); Rom. 11:2 ("God has not cast off his people whom he foreknew"); 1 Pet. 1:2 ("elect strangers according to the Father's foreknowledge, unto sanctification of the Spirit…"). From these they infer that God elected to glory those he foreknew would be conformed to the Son's image — holy and good — so that foresight of future goodness or holiness was the cause of election to glory.
source_text: Secundo, urgentur illa loca in quibus electio sive praedestinatio ad gloriam expressis verbis conjungitur cum praescientia. Ut Rom. viii. 29, 30. Quos praescivit, eos & praedestinavit ut conformes fiant imagini Filii sui, &c. Et Rom. xi. 2. Non repulit Deus plebem suam quam praescivit. Et 1. Pet. i. 2. Electis advenis secundum praescientiam Dei Patris in sanctificationem spiritus, &c. Ex hisce & hujusmodi locis inferunt adversarii, Deum eos ad gloriam elegisse, quos praescivit futuros conformes imagini Filii sui, id est, sanctos & bonos; ita ut haec praescientia futurae bonitatis sive sanctitatis fuerit causa electionis ad gloriam.
